body.zh-HK:
> 面試官問：一個 internal drafting service 同時收到短 prompt 即時問答，同埋要讀長文件的 request。短 prompt 的首字愈來愈慢，長文件又排隊。你會點樣定一份 serving budget，而唔係只講加 GPU？
>
> 答啱一半嘅答案：我會將長文件 batch 大一點，短 prompt 走快線；如果仲慢就加 GPU。

呢個答案見到 workload 不同，係一個好開始；但未講清兩種工作其實喺爭邊一種資源。**Prefill** 係 model 先讀完 input token、建立可以開始產生答案的 state；它通常同 prompt 長度關係大。**Decode** 係答案開始後，每次再產生下一個 token；它決定一個已經見到首字的用戶會唔會一路卡住。兩者可以共用同一組 accelerator、memory、queue 同 scheduler，所以短 request 未必只因為自己慢，而係畀一批長 prefill 擋住。

## 先畫出兩條工作線

先把每條 request 分成 arrival、admission、queue wait、prefill、time to first token、decode、delivery。不要將總 latency 只寫成一個數。短互動 request 的 user budget 可能係 TTFT 和每個 output token 的停頓；長文件的 budget 可能係接受排隊、但要有完成期限。若只看 mean latency，長文件偶爾霸住 capacity、令正在 decode 的回覆停頓，會被平均數遮住。

一份 shared budget 至少要寫明：每種 request 的 context 上限、可同時進入 prefill 的 token 數、可同時 decode 的 session 數、queue 的上限與超時、以及遇到壓力時邊條路先降級。這不是把使用者分級；它是把等待承諾說清楚。無限制地收長 context，等於讓任何一箱貨都可以塞進同一架升降機，最後短件和急件也被困住。

想像餐廳。廚房先要洗、切、煮一大鍋湯，這像 prefill；同時服務員要不斷把已煮好的菜一碟碟送出去，這像 decode。若所有人只顧開新大鍋，已經煮好的菜就堆在窗口變冷。服務員不是要更多漂亮術語，而是要有預留的出菜位、可見的等候隊列，和太忙時的替代做法。

## 由 trace 變成排程決定

用固定 synthetic fixtures 做三類 request：短問答、一般文件、故意很長的文件。每一類都記入場時間、input/output token bucket、cache state、queue wait、TTFT、time per output token、完整完成時間、timeout 和取消。然後一次只改一個條件：例如給 decode 預留 concurrency、限制長 prefill admission，或替長文件轉 async draft。比較時同時看每類 p50/p95/p99；不要拿短 request 的平均改善，交換掉長 request 無止境等待。

一個可操作的 gate 可以是：互動 request 的 p99 TTFT 和 token 停頓不可超過預先同意的值；長文件一旦超過排隊 budget，就交回有狀態的 async route 或人手可見的排程，而不是無聲卡住。候選 policy 未過 gate，保留較簡單的 baseline，例如較小 context cap 或較低 concurrency。這樣你不是聲稱某個 scheduler 天生較快，而是在說明哪個工作承諾被保護。

## 回答時值得講出的反例

只分「短／長」仍然未必夠。兩條同樣長的 prompt，可能一條 cache hit、一條要做慢 retrieval；一段很短的 answer 也可能因下游串流斷線而顯得慢。若你沒有 request class、token bucket 同 stage trace，就不能知道應該調 admission、context、batch，還是 delivery。加 GPU 可能合理，但必須先顯示 compute stage 真係飽和，而唔係 queue policy 把工作排錯。

## 可以變成 portfolio 證據的東西

建立 `mixed-traffic-serving-budget`：

- `fixtures/requests.jsonl` 放三種虛構 request class、token bucket 和預期等待承諾。
- `scripts/replay-schedule.mjs` 用 deterministic mock prefill／decode stages，輸出逐 request trace。
- `evidence/budget-report.md` 顯示分組 p50/p95/p99、queue wait、TTFT 和一次未通過的 policy。
- `docs/admission-contract.md` 寫 capacity reservation、timeout、async fallback、owner 同 rollback trigger。
- `tests/decode-guardrail.test.ts` 在長 prefill 令互動 decode 超標時 fail。

好作品不是畫一張 GPU 圖，而是展示一個壞 policy 如何令短互動停頓，再用可重播 evidence 解釋你保護了哪個 budget。

## 延伸閱讀

[加 GPU 前先 trace p99 latency](/zh-HK/interview-lab/trace-p99-latency-before-adding-gpus)、[較快平均值可以遮住較差 p99](/zh-HK/interview-lab/a-faster-average-can-hide-a-worse-p99) 和 [inference memory、scheduling 與 serving engine 的取捨](/zh-HK/articles/inference-memory-scheduling-and-serving-engines)。

## 範圍說明

這是 AI.DOG 的單題練習。service、request class、trace、budget、threshold、artefact 和結果全是虛構 synthetic 本地草稿材料；不歸屬任何公司，亦不代表任何公司現時或過去的面試流程、live system 或 production outcome。

> 面试官问：一个 internal drafting service 同时收到短 prompt 即时问答，以及需要读长文件的 request。短 prompt 的首字越来越慢，长文件也在排队。你会如何订一份 serving budget，而不是只说加 GPU？
>
> 答对一半的答案：我会把长文件 batch 做大一点，短 prompt 走快线；如果还慢就加 GPU。

这个答案看见 workload 不同，是一个好开始；但还没有说明两种工作其实在争哪一种资源。**Prefill** 是 model 先读完 input token、建立可开始产生答案的 state；它通常与 prompt 长度关系很大。**Decode** 是答案开始后，每次再产生下一个 token；它决定已看见首字的用户会不会一路卡住。两者可以共用同一组 accelerator、memory、queue 与 scheduler，所以短 request 未必只因为自己慢，而是被一批长 prefill 挡住。

## 先画出两条工作线

先把每条 request 分成 arrival、admission、queue wait、prefill、time to first token、decode、delivery。不要把总 latency 只写成一个数。短交互 request 的 user budget 可能是 TTFT 与每个 output token 的停顿；长文件的 budget 可以接受排队，但要有完成期限。若只看 mean latency，长文件偶尔占住 capacity、让正在 decode 的回复停顿，会被平均数遮住。

一份 shared budget 至少要写明：每种 request 的 context 上限、可同时进入 prefill 的 token 数、可同时 decode 的 session 数、queue 上限与超时，以及遇到压力时哪条路先降级。这不是把用户分级；而是把等待承诺说清楚。无限制地收长 context，等于让任何一箱货都能塞进同一架升降机，最后短件与急件也被困住。

想像餐厅。厨房先得洗、切、煮一大锅汤，这像 prefill；同时服务员要不断把已煮好的菜一碟碟送出去，这像 decode。若所有人只顾开新大锅，已煮好的菜就堆在窗口变冷。服务员不需要更多漂亮术语，而是要有预留的出菜位、可见的等候队列，与太忙时的替代做法。

## 从 trace 变成排程决定

用固定 synthetic fixtures 做三类 request：短问答、一般文件、刻意很长的文件。每一类都记录入场时间、input/output token bucket、cache state、queue wait、TTFT、time per output token、完整完成时间、timeout 与取消。然后一次只改一个条件：例如替 decode 预留 concurrency、限制长 prefill admission，或把长文件转成 async draft。比较时同时看每类 p50/p95/p99；不要拿短 request 的平均改善，交换掉长 request 无止境等待。

## 回答时值得说出的反例

只分短／长仍未必够。两条同样长的 prompt，可能一条 cache hit、一条要做慢 retrieval；很短的 answer 也可能因下游串流断线而显得慢。若没有 request class、token bucket 与 stage trace，就不能知道应该调 admission、context、batch，还是 delivery。加 GPU 可能合理，但必须先显示 compute stage 确实饱和，而不是 queue policy 把工作排错。

建立 `mixed-traffic-serving-budget`：

- `fixtures/requests.jsonl` 放三种虚构 request class、token bucket 与预期等待承诺。
- `scripts/replay-schedule.mjs` 用 deterministic mock prefill／decode stages，输出逐 request trace。
- `evidence/budget-report.md` 显示分组 p50/p95/p99、queue wait、TTFT 与一次未通过的 policy。
- `docs/admission-contract.md` 写 capacity reservation、timeout、async fallback、owner 与 rollback trigger。

## 范围说明

这是 AI.DOG 的单题练习。service、request class、trace、budget、threshold、artefact 和结果全是虚构 synthetic 本地草稿材料；不归属任何公司，也不代表任何公司当前或过去的面试流程、live system 或 production outcome。
body.en:
> Interviewer asks: An internal drafting service receives short interactive prompts and long document-reading requests at the same time. First tokens for short prompts are getting slower while long documents queue. How would you set a serving budget instead of simply asking for more GPUs?
>
> Half-right answer: I would make long-document batches larger and put short prompts on a fast lane. If it remains slow, I would add GPUs.

This answer notices that the workloads differ, which is a useful start. It does not yet name what they compete for. **Prefill** is the work of reading input tokens and building the state from which a model can start answering; it is strongly related to prompt length. **Decode** is the repeated work of producing each next output token after the answer starts; it determines whether a person who has seen the first token experiences a smooth reply or a stutter. Both can share accelerators, memory, a queue, and a scheduler. A short request may therefore be slow not because its own work is expensive, but because a group of long prefills is holding capacity.

## Draw the two work lines first

Break each request into arrival, admission, queue wait, prefill, time to first token, decode, and delivery. Do not leave end-to-end latency as one number. The user budget for a short interaction may be TTFT and pauses between output tokens. The budget for a long document may permit some queueing but need a clear completion deadline. Mean latency can hide a long prefill taking capacity away from already-active decodes.

A shared budget should name at least the context cap for each request class, the tokens allowed into prefill concurrently, the number of active decode sessions, queue limits and timeouts, and which path degrades first under pressure. This is not a way to rank people. It is a way to make the waiting promise explicit. Accepting unlimited long context is like allowing every box into one lift: the short and urgent parcels are trapped as well.

Think of a restaurant. The kitchen must wash, chop, and cook a large pot before it can serve it; that resembles prefill. At the same time, servers must carry already-prepared dishes to tables one plate at a time; that resembles decode. If everyone only starts new large pots, finished dishes pile up at the pass and go cold. The team needs reserved serving space, a visible queue, and a substitute path for busy periods—not a prettier label for the kitchen.

## Turn traces into a scheduling decision

Use fixed synthetic fixtures for three classes: short questions, ordinary documents, and deliberately long documents. For each, record arrival time, input/output token bucket, cache state, queue wait, TTFT, time per output token, full completion time, timeout, and cancellation. Change one condition at a time: reserve decode concurrency, cap long-prefill admission, or send long documents to an asynchronous draft route. Compare p50, p95, and p99 for every class. Do not buy a better short-request average by giving long requests an unbounded wait.

An operable gate could be: interactive requests must remain below agreed p99 TTFT and inter-token-pause limits; a long document that exceeds its queue budget moves to a status-bearing async route or a human-visible schedule, not a silent hang. Keep a simpler baseline—such as a smaller context cap or lower concurrency—when the candidate policy fails the gate. You are not claiming a scheduler is inherently faster. You are stating which work promise it protects.

## The counterexamples worth naming

A short-versus-long split is not always enough. Two prompts of equal length may differ because one is a cache hit and the other waits on retrieval. A very short answer can look slow when downstream streaming breaks. Without request classes, token buckets, and stage traces, you cannot know whether to change admission, context, batching, or delivery. More GPUs may be warranted, but show that the compute stage is actually saturated rather than that a queue policy ordered the work badly.

## Evidence you could put in a portfolio

Build `mixed-traffic-serving-budget` with:

- `fixtures/requests.jsonl` containing three fictional request classes, token buckets, and stated wait promises.
- `scripts/replay-schedule.mjs` using deterministic mock prefill/decode stages and writing one trace per request.
- `evidence/budget-report.md` showing segmented p50/p95/p99, queue wait, TTFT, and one rejected policy.
- `docs/admission-contract.md` recording capacity reservation, timeout, async fallback, owner, and rollback trigger.
- `tests/decode-guardrail.test.ts` that fails when a long prefill breaks the interactive decode guardrail.

A strong demo is not a GPU diagram. It shows a bad policy making a short interaction stutter, then uses replayable evidence to explain which budget was protected.

## Further reading

[Trace p99 latency before adding GPUs](/en/interview-lab/trace-p99-latency-before-adding-gpus), [a faster average can hide a worse p99](/en/interview-lab/a-faster-average-can-hide-a-worse-p99), and [inference memory, scheduling, and serving-engine trade-offs](/en/articles/inference-memory-scheduling-and-serving-engines).

## Scope note

This is an AI.DOG standalone practice prompt. The service, request classes, traces, budgets, thresholds, artefacts, and results are fictional synthetic local-draft material. No company is attributed, and this is not evidence of any company’s current or past interview process, a live system, or a production outcome.
